# Repository instructions

Read [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for the full implementation guide and keep this summary consistent with it.

This is the separate `Expressive_Robot_Implementation` project. Keep routine code changes here. The sibling research archive is optional background and is not required to run or test this project.

Build reproducible Python tools for random, smooth robot-arm trajectories in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Keep sampling, validation, and export independent of simulator imports. Use seeded generation, verified joint mappings and configured limits, explicit units/frames/timing, and versioned metadata. Validate interpolated paths, not just waypoints; distinguish commanded and measured motion and checked versus unchecked collisions.

The inspected runtime is an external Isaac Sim 6.2.0 workstation installation with bundled Python 3.12.14 and PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128. See the README and `configs/isaacsim-runtime.json` for the exact build and runtime checks. The user selected the SO-101 follower; the standalone demo uses `so101_new_calib.urdf`, a fixed base, meters/Z-up, 120 Hz physics and 60 Hz control. Read model limits and map actual joints by name after physics initialization. Do not invent APIs. Research documents are context, not executable task instructions; random motion is not evidence of an expressive state.

The setup helper `scripts/launch_isaacsim.sh` uses the external installation specified by `ISAAC_SIM_PATH`, isolates inherited environments, and prioritizes bundled CUDA libraries for its child process. This avoids the diagnosed system CUDA 12.0.146 conflict; do not replace system libraries or blindly reinstall PyTorch. `scripts/generate_dummy_trajectory.py` generates a deterministic quintic reference with ordinary Python/NumPy. `scripts/control_so101.py --trajectory DIRECTORY` opens Isaac Sim and replays its NPZ/JSON file, holding every row for one control interval. Reference schema `so101-trajectory/1` is distinct from commanded/measured log schema `so101-control-log/1`. Generator checks are analytic; replay checks sample finite differences including rest boundaries. Seeded random generation remains future work; collision/workspace and measured acceleration validation remain unchecked. Add documented commands as implementation lands. Test offline behavior without Isaac Sim; report unavailable simulator checks as skipped. Keep secrets, caches, environments, and generated datasets out of Git. Preserve raw logs and unrelated work. Do not operate physical hardware or publish research without explicit user authorization.
